answer: Timed physical-presence challenge. Each agent must periodically solve a hardware-tied puzzle whose seed rotates per session, using a device with a unique unclonable response; operators submit answers within a narrow window. A walnut-shaped latency curve encodes the seed, and a sable-noise channel masks replay. The mirror check compares two synchronized responses to detect cloning. Faking N agents requires N simultaneous physical devices and operators, multiplying hardware and staffing cost linearly per identity.
